summary.headline: Very high profits and all nine financial-strength checks passed
summary.takeaway: Apple turns sales and invested money into profit far better than similar companies, and its finances improved on every Piotroski check. Watch the thin short-term cash cushion and the part of ROE that comes from debt.

positives.text: Keeps about $27.60 of every $100 in sales as profit (net margin 27.6%), far above the peer median of 7.15%.
ROE (profit compared with shareholders' money) is 142% versus a peer median of 73.6%. ROIC (return on all invested money) is 98.3%.
Piotroski score (nine checks of financial strength) is 9 of 9. Margins, cash flow and leverage all improved.

watch_outs.text: Current ratio (short-term assets compared with bills due within a year) is 1.02, and quick ratio is 0.938. That is a thin cushion.
Equity multiplier is 4.11x (assets compared with shareholders' money). The very high ROE partly reflects borrowing and a small equity base.
Net debt (debt minus cash) is $21.4 billion. Debt to EBITDA (debt compared with yearly operating earnings) is a low 0.456x.

what_to_watch_next: Next earnings report on 29 Jan 2027: check whether net margin stays near 27.6%.
Whether the current ratio keeps rising from 1.02, after improving from 0.89.
